clue.text: Lay down before writer

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a scribe is a copyist or writer

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something down in front of an author.
explanation.definitionFit: To prescribe a rule is to set it down with authority.

clue.text: One in a hurry, say, to get to the country

indicators.note: say tells the solver the preceding phrase is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: someone who rushes is a rusher

explanation.surface: A hasty traveller trying to reach a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSHER, as spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the name of the vast Eurasian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest nation on Earth by area, spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Plan is altered for sort of column

indicators.note: altered means the letters of the two words before it are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A scheme is revised to suit a kind of pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone is called the spinal or vertebral column.

clue.text: Teased, being badly dressed

explanation.surface: Someone mocked for wearing shabby clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease them, and ragged clothes are torn and shabby, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Stick with unadventurous team, and take extra care

explanation.surface: Advice to back a cautious squad and play it carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: to belong to (be on) a team that plays safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting cautiously to avoid risk; read literally it is joining a side that is safe.

clue.text: Excel, being prepared like a beggar

parts.note: to cap is to top or outdo, so excel
something in hand is arranged or under preparation

explanation.surface: Someone excels while getting ready, as a pauper might.
explanation.definitionFit: A humble pleader holds out a hat for alms, hence the idiom for asking humbly.

clue.text: Went down with minor illness — about to expire

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a cold is a common minor ailment
a policy or right that lapses expires

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill with a cold, as if close to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to expire' reads as 'close to death', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down suddenly.

clue.text: Parents' increasing ability?

parts.note: read as a skill improving, it is really the power of parents to increase their number by having children

explanation.surface: Asking whether mothers and fathers are getting more capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecundity is the capacity to produce offspring, increasing the family.

clue.text: A line in a bit of opera

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the next one

parts.note: some means a bit, a certain amount

explanation.surface: A single lyric appearing in an extract from an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss's one-act opera based on Oscar Wilde's play.

clue.text: Is fish not about in this area of London?

parts.note: ling is a long cod-like sea fish

indicators.note: about tells the solver to turn the word not round so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A question whether fish is absent around a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in north London, home of Arsenal football club.

clue.text: Log is in quarters

explanation.surface: Firewood stored in living accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is both a thick chunk of firewood and lodging assigned to soldiers.

clue.text: Weed — get it removed with care

indicators.note: removed is read as moved again, so the letters of the surrounding words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: pull out the weed carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges GETIT and CARE together; 'Weed' is slang for tobacco, here a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Weed is old slang for tobacco, and a cigarette is a rolled smoke of it.

clue.text: Where print unions used to worship?

definitions.text: Where print unions used to worship?

parts.words: Where print unions used to worship?
parts.note: a printers' union branch was traditionally called by the name of a small place of worship, so the clue plays on both senses

explanation.surface: A question about the religious habits of printing trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of a printing trade union is traditionally so named, as well as a small church.

clue.text: Two boys of an age, younger than Victoria

definitions.text: of an age, younger than Victoria

parts.note: Edward and Ian are two boys' names
Edward and Ian are two boys' names

explanation.surface: Two young lads of similar age, both junior to a girl called Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edwardian era (1901-10) came after the Victorian.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of Edward VII's reign followed Queen Victoria's.

clue.text: Spears one's food

parts.note: read as stabbing food with a fork, it is really a vegetable eaten in tender shoots called spears

explanation.surface: Someone stabs their dinner with a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable whose edible shoots are known as spears.

clue.text: Signal for departure of miserable lord — about time

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling miserable

indicators.note: about means the word for lord goes round the time letter

parts.note: a peer is a lord

explanation.surface: A sign marking the exit of an unhappy nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Also the name of a long-running BBC children's TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue and white flag hoisted in port to show a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Thus announced work on repair

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so what is heard is written differently

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An instruction, so declared, to get on with mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching with needle and thread is how torn cloth is mended.

clue.text: Contribution to boat

explanation.surface: A donation towards a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub is a subscription paid, and also short for submarine.

clue.text: Not altogether with humour

indicators.note: not altogether means the following word is incomplete, its last letter missing

explanation.surface: A remark that one is not entirely amused.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is cleverness with words that amuses.

clue.text: Loss of belief in conjuring act?

definitions.text: Loss of belief in conjuring act?

parts.words: Loss of belief in conjuring act?
parts.note: read as becoming sceptical of magic, it splits into removing (dis-) the trick (illusion)

explanation.surface: A spectator stops believing in a magic show.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming disenchanted, having one's false ideas stripped away.

clue.text: Flying club?

parts.note: read as an aviation society, it is really a winged animal that shares its name with a sports club used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: A society for amateur pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying mammal shares its name with the wooden implement used in cricket and baseball.

clue.text: Went down in a cot, holding a thumb at first

indicators.note: holding means the bed word contains the next letters

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of thumb

explanation.surface: A baby in a cot, sucking its thumb, settles down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts AT (A plus the T from 'thumb') inside BED, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm or pain that abated subsided or lessened.

clue.text: One much disliking accepting money for rope

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the letter in

parts.note: a hater is someone who dislikes intensely
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for the pound

explanation.surface: A bitter person taking a bribe for a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a rope or strap for leading a horse, or a hangman's noose.

clue.text: Her mate is all eyes for her

definitions.text: Her mate is all eyes for her

parts.words: Her mate is all eyes for her
parts.note: read as a devoted partner, it is a bird whose mate has a tail covered in eye-spots

explanation.surface: A doting partner who cannot take his eyes off her.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the bird whose male displays a tail patterned with eyes.

clue.text: Stupidly fails to keep note for last exams

indicators.note: to keep means the shuffled letters hold another inside them
stupidly signals that the letters of fails are jumbled

explanation.surface: A student fails through foolishness and must sit end-of-year tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' rearranges FAILS as FIALS; 'to keep' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Finals are the closing examinations of a degree course.

clue.text: From group of animals, horse comes between me and lake

indicators.note: comes between places the horse word between the other two pieces

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Within a zoo collection, a horse lies between a person and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show.

clue.text: Trader who holds all the cards

explanation.surface: A merchant with total control of the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer trades goods, and is also the person dealing out the playing cards.

clue.text: The opposite of costing the earth?

definitions.text: The opposite of costing the earth?

parts.words: The opposite of costing the earth?
parts.note: costing the earth means very expensive; the opposite is very cheap, with the earth punned as soil

explanation.surface: A question about what is the reverse of exorbitantly priced.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning extremely inexpensive, playing on earth as soil.

clue.text: People taken with a copper's astuteness

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men means people

explanation.surface: Folk impressed by a policeman's sharp wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewdness, the ability to judge well.

clue.text: Caution swallowing ecstasy — it makes for exhaustion

indicators.note: swallowing means the caution word takes the drug letter inside

parts.note: wariness is caution
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Warning that taking ecstasy leads to burnout.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness is tiredness, being worn out.
